mainTopic: How שעטנז teaches that an עשה pushes aside a לא תעשה, and why עליה is needed to block an עשה from pushing aside a לאו with כרת
overview: This amud first finishes defending the idea that the side-by-side פסוקים of שעטנז and גדילים (דברים 22:11-12) can teach a lesson. A lesson like that needs a free, extra word. The גמרא tries 'גדילים', then 'צמר ופשתים יחדו', then 'שעטנז'. Each time it is pushed back, because the word has its own job. In the end it says the unusual word שעטנז carries everything, both the rule that the material must be combed, spun and twisted (שוע, טווי, נוז) and the link that teaches that an עשה pushes aside a plain לא תעשה. Then the גמרא asks why the word עליה was needed to stop יבום with a wife's sister, since we have no source that an עשה can push aside a לאו with כרת. It tries to learn such a source from מילה, פסח and תמיד, alone and in pairs and all together, and rejects every option. It then answers that we might have learned it from כיבוד אב ואם, and brings a ברייתא about honoring parents and שבת. The גמרא suggests reading that ברייתא as a father asking for real שבת labor, begins to reject that reading, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: They learn it from the first verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes answering the question just before this section: the source is the first verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from the first verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer to a question asked right before this section. The source for the point is 'the first verse.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion asked how the רבנן know that כלאים is allowed in ציצית. The answer is that they learn it from the first verse, meaning the side-by-side פסוקים of שעטנז and גדילים. The next steps defend that this pair of פסוקים really has a free word that can teach a lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: From the first verse

phrases.english: From the first verse.
phrases.notes: The 'first verse' is the side-by-side פסוקים, which teach that כלאים is allowed in ציצית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the question asked just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does this idea come from?

steps.title: The word 'twisted fringes' is extra, so it is free
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said 'make ציצית for yourself.' Saying 'גדילים' instead shows the word is free for a lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say 'You shall make ציצית for yourself.' Why do I need 'twisted fringes'? Learn from it that it is free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the word 'גדילים' is extra. An extra word means the side-by-side פסוקים can be used to teach a lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lesson from two פסוקים that sit next to each other (סמוכים) needs a word that is not needed for anything else. The גמרא argues that the תורה could have used the plain word 'ציצית.' Using 'גדילים' instead makes that word free (מופנה).

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the verse say
Twisted fringes (the word in דברים 22:12)
Why do I need it? (this word seems extra)
To be 'free': an extra word left open for a lesson

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the pattern repeated through the whole section: find the extra word, and show it is free.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
"You shall make ציצית for yourself,"
Why do I need "twisted fringes"?
Learn from this that it is free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to defend the lesson taught by the side-by-side פסוקים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every word is needed, so no lesson can come from the side-by-side פסוקים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'גדילים' is extra and free for the lesson.

steps.title: 'Twisted fringes' teaches the number of strings
steps.stepSummary: The challenge: 'גדילים' is not extra. It teaches how many strings ציצית needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: This word comes to teach the amount. 'Twisted fringe' means two strings, and 'twisted fringes' means four. Make a twisted fringe and fold it over from the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. The word 'גדילים' has its own job, which is teaching how many strings to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single 'גדיל' (twisted cord) needs at least two strings. The plural 'גדילים' means four. Folding the four over in the middle makes eight. Since the word teaches this, it is not free.

keyTerms.meaning: For the amount or measure
One twisted cord (at least two strings)
And fold it over from its middle

phrases.english: This comes to teach the amount:
"Twisted fringe" means two,
"twisted fringes" means four:
Make a twisted fringe and fold it over from its middle!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 2's claim that 'גדילים' is extra.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word teaches the number of strings, so it is not extra.

steps.title: 'Wool and linen together' is extra, so it is free
steps.stepSummary: The answer moves to the other פסוק. It could have said only 'do not wear שעטנז,' so 'צמר ופשתים יחדו' is free.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say 'Do not wear שעטנז.' Why do I need 'wool and linen together'? Learn from it that it is free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that 'גדילים' has a job. It finds an extra word in the כלאים פסוק instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is enough for one of the two side-by-side פסוקים to have a free word. 'שעטנז' alone already tells us the prohibition. So 'צמר ופשתים יחדו' looks extra and is free for the lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden mix of wool and linen in clothing
Wool and linen together
You shall not wear

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say:
"You shall not wear שעטנז,"
why do I need "wool and linen together"?
Learn from this that it is free.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לֵימָא קְרָא לֹא תִלְבַּשׁ שַׁעַטְנֵז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 3 by finding a free word in the other פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the free word to the neighboring פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'גדילים' is used up, so there is no free word.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'צמר ופשתים יחדו' is extra and free.

steps.title: 'Together' teaches the two-stitch rule
steps.stepSummary: The challenge: 'צמר ופשתים יחדו' is needed to teach that two stitches join the materials and one stitch does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, it is needed to teach this: if one stitches two stitches, that counts as joining. One stitch does not count as joining.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again. 'Wool and linen together' also has its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יחדו' (together) teaches when wool and linen count as attached. Two stitches make them attached and forbidden. One stitch does not. So these words are not free either.

keyTerms.meaning: And still
It is needed (for another lesson)
A stitch
Attachment (counts as joined)

phrases.english: But still, it is needed:
for one who stitches two stitches, it is attachment,
phrases.notes: This rule comes from the word 'יחדו' (together).

phrases.english: and one stitch is not attachment!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 4's claim that 'צמר ופשתים יחדו' is free.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'צמר ופשתים יחדו' is free
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase teaches the two-stitch rule, so it is not extra.

steps.title: The word 'שעטנז' itself is extra, so it is free
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the תורה could have written 'do not wear wool and linen together.' So the word 'שעטנז' is free.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the Merciful One write 'Do not wear wool and linen together.' Why do I need 'שעטנז'? Learn from it that it is free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the question around. If 'wool and linen together' is needed, then the word 'שעטנז' is the extra one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'צמר ופשתים יחדו' is used for the stitch rule, that phrase alone already states the prohibition. So 'שעטנז' seems to add nothing new and to be free. The next step challenges this.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Merciful One (the תורה) write

steps.whatToRemember: Each time a word is shown to have a job, the גמרא finds another word that is extra. Here 'שעטנז' looks free. The next step shows it has its own job, and in the end the גמרא says the unusual word שעטנז carries both lessons. So the side-by-side פסוקים of כלאים and ציצית can be used to teach the lesson.

phrases.english: If so, let the Merciful One write:
"You shall not wear wool and linen together,"
why do I need "שעטנז"?
Learn from this that it is free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5 by showing the word 'שעטנז' is the extra one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both 'גדילים' and 'צמר ופשתים יחדו' are used up, so nothing is free.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שעטנז' is extra, so the lesson from the side-by-side פסוקים stands.

steps.title: The word שעטנז is also needed for another rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the word שעטנז is not free. It teaches that כלאים only applies when the material is combed, spun and twisted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the word שעטנז is still needed to teach that the material must be combed, spun and twisted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 6. It says the word שעטנז already has its own lesson, so it is not free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said שעטנז was an extra word, free to teach the link to ציצית. Now the גמרא points out that שעטנז is read as three words joined together: שוע (combed), טווי (spun), נוז (twisted). Without all three, it is not the forbidden mix. So the word seems to be busy and not free.

keyTerms.meaning: And still / but still
It is needed for it (for another lesson)
Combed smooth
Spun into thread
Twisted or joined together

phrases.english: But it is still needed for this:
it is not forbidden until it is combed, spun, and twisted!
phrases.notes: The word שעטנז is split into three pieces: שע, טנ, נז. Each piece stands for one of these steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 6's claim that the word שעטנז is free.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שעטנז is an extra word free for a lesson
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שעטנז is already used as a short form for שוע, טווי, נוז, so it is not free.

steps.title: Both lessons come from the word שעטנז
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that everything is learned from שעטנז. The unusual word is enough for both the 'combed, spun, twisted' rule and the link to ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the whole thing comes from the word שעטנז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. One unusual word, שעטנז, carries both lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of hunting for a different extra word, the גמרא says שעטנז is strange enough to do two jobs. It gives the rule about combed, spun and twisted material, and it also gives the link between the ציצית פסוק and the כלאים פסוק. That link is the source that an עשה pushes aside a לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we change our answer)
All of it, the whole teaching
It comes out from, it is learned from

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that an עשה pushes aside a regular לא תעשה is learned from ציצית and כלאים, and the word שעטנז carries the whole lesson.

phrases.english: Rather: all of it
comes out from the word 'שעטנז'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7 by letting one word teach both lessons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: One unusual word teaches more than one lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each lesson needs its own separate extra word, so שעטנז seems used up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word שעטנז is unusual enough to carry both the 'combed, spun, twisted' rule and the link to ציצית.

steps.title: Why would we think an עשה beats a לאו with כרת?
steps.stepSummary: We have a source that an עשה pushes aside a plain לאו. But where do we see it push aside a לאו with כרת, so that the תורה had to write עליה to stop יבום with a wife's sister?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found that an עשה pushes aside a plain לא תעשה. But where do we find that it pushes aside a לא תעשה with כרת, so that the word עליה was needed to forbid her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It asks why the תורה needed the word עליה at all, since we have no source that an עשה could beat a לאו with כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said the word עליה teaches that the מצוה of יבום does not push aside the איסור of a wife's sister. But the source from ציצית only covers a plain לאו. Without a source that an עשה could ever beat a כרת-level לאו, we would never think יבום could beat it, so why was עליה needed?

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (we have a source)
Plain, alone, only
Being cut off, a very severe punishment
Where?
'With her', the extra word in the פסוק about a wife's sister

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether an עשה beats a כרת-level לאו. It is asking why we would ever have thought it does, since that is why the word עליה would be needed.

phrases.english: We have found that a positive מצוה comes
and pushes aside a plain prohibition.
A prohibition that carries כרת:
where do we find that it pushes it aside,
so that 'עליה' was needed to forbid her?
phrases.notes: This points back to the extra word in ויקרא 18:18, which the גמרא used earlier to forbid יבום with a wife's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן דְּאָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה גְּרֵידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the finished source for a plain לאו and asks about a לאו with כרת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word עליה to forbid יבום with a wife's sister
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no source that an עשה beats a לאו with כרת, so no word should be needed to block it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides whether an עשה could ever push aside a כרת-level איסור. That is the background for the whole discussion of יבום with עריות.

steps.title: We cannot learn from מילה
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say we learn from מילה, which is done on שבת even though breaking שבת carries כרת. The גמרא rejects this because מילה is special: thirteen covenants were made over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say, let us learn from מילה: what about מילה, over which thirteen covenants were made!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries מילה as a source and turns it down. מילה is too special to be the model for other מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה on the eighth day pushes aside שבת, and breaking שבת carries כרת. So it looks like a case of an עשה beating a כרת-level לאו. But מילה has unusual weight, with thirteen covenants, so we cannot assume that a regular עשה like יבום has the same power.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say
Let us learn
What about...? (a way of showing the source is special)
Covenants

phrases.english: And if you say: let us learn it from מילה:
what about מילה,
since over it were made
thirteen covenants!
phrases.notes: The word ברית comes up thirteen times in the מילה chapter, בראשית 17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to Step 9's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects מילה as the source that an עשה beats a לאו with כרת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מילה is unusually important, with thirteen covenants, so other מצוות cannot be learned from it.

steps.title: We cannot learn from פסח either
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest learning from קרבן פסח, which is brought on שבת. The גמרא rejects this because פסח is itself a מצוה with כרת for not doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: From פסח? What about פסח, which carries כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries קרבן פסח as a source and turns it down too. פסח is special because skipping it carries כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering the פסח pushes aside שבת, a לאו with כרת. But פסח is an unusual עשה, since a person who does not bring it gets כרת. So it is not a fair model for a regular עשה like יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרבן פסח, the Pesach offering
Since, because it has

steps.whatToRemember: Both possible sources, מילה and פסח, are rejected because each is a special, extra-strong עשה. The גמרא keeps searching for a source, and step 16 gives its answer for why עליה was needed.

phrases.english: And if from פסח:
what about פסח, which carries כרת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting מילה, tries פסח and rejects it in the same way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects פסח as the source that an עשה beats a לאו with כרת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: פסח is an עשה that itself carries כרת, so it is stronger than an ordinary עשה.

steps.title: The daily offering is rejected because it is frequent
steps.stepSummary: Someone suggests learning from the קרבן תמיד, which is brought even on שבת. The גמרא rejects this because the תמיד happens every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe learn it from the daily offering? No. The daily offering is special because it is constant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third source, the קרבן תמיד, which is brought on שבת even though breaking שבת carries כרת. It rejects this right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצוה done every single day may be stronger than an ordinary מצוה. So the fact that the תמיד pushes aside שבת does not prove that every עשה, such as יבום, can push aside a כרת prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offering brought in the בית המקדש every morning and afternoon
Frequent, happening regularly
'What about...?' A formula that points out a special feature so a comparison fails

phrases.english: From the daily offering?
phrases.notes: The suggestion is to learn from the תמיד, which is brought even on שבת.

phrases.english: What about the daily offering, which is frequent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third single source tried and rejected, after מילה and פסח
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the rule from תמיד alone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תמיד is frequent, so it may have extra power that other מצוות lack

steps.title: Try learning from two cases together
steps.stepSummary: Since no single case works, the גמרא suggests combining two of them and asks which pair to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: It cannot be learned from one. Let it be learned from two. From which two?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא proposes pairing two sources together, then asks which pair could work, and the next steps test each pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When each source has its own special feature, combining two can sometimes cancel those features out. Then only the shared feature, being an עשה that pushes aside כרת, would remain. The question now is whether any pair has no special shared feature.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot be learned from one source
Let it be learned from two sources together
From which one should it be learned?

phrases.english: From one it cannot come,
let it come from two:
From which ones should it come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all single sources failed, shifts to learning from a combination
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which pair of sources can teach that an עשה pushes aside a כרת prohibition

steps.title: The first two pairs share special features
steps.stepSummary: מילה with פסח both carry כרת if not done. פסח with תמיד are both needs of the altar. So neither pair works.
steps.simpleTranslation: From מילה and פסח? They both carry כרת. From פסח and תמיד? They are both needs of the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests two pairs and rejects both. Each pair shares a special quality that ordinary מצוות like יבום do not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה and פסח are both מצוות whose neglect carries כרת, so they are extra serious. פסח and תמיד are both offerings for the מזבח, so they serve 'הגבוה‎', ה׳, and not a person's own needs. A special shared feature means the pair cannot teach about a regular עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Circumcision
The קרבן פסח, the Pesach offering
Spiritual cutting off, a severe divine punishment
A need of the Most High, meaning something for the מזבח and the בית המקדש

phrases.english: From circumcision and the Pesach offering?
They both carry כרת!
From the Pesach offering and the daily offering?
They are both a need of the Most High.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first two possible pairs from step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the pairs מילה+פסח and פסח+תמיד
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each pair shares a special feature: כרת for neglect, or service of the מזבח

steps.title: The last pair and all three together fail too
steps.stepSummary: מילה and תמיד were both given before the תורה was given at סיני. The same is true of all three together, so no combination works.
steps.simpleTranslation: From מילה and תמיד? They both existed before מתן תורה. This follows the view that the עולה that ישראל brought in the desert was the עולת תמיד. And from all of them too? They all existed before מתן תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the last pair, and then even all three together. Every one of these מצוות was already commanded before מתן תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצוות given before סיני form their own special group, so they cannot teach about a later מצוה like יבום. That the תמיד came before סיני depends on one opinion: the עולה brought at סיני was the עולת תמיד. So every combination is blocked, and the search for a source fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the Divine speech, meaning before the תורה was given at סיני
According to the one who says
A burnt offering
And from all of them as well

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 'לפני הדבור' means these מצוות are no longer binding. It only means they were commanded before סיני, which gives them a special status that blocks the comparison.

phrases.english: From circumcision and the daily offering?
They both existed before the Divine speech,
phrases.notes: He means before the תורה was given at סיני.

phrases.english: and this follows the one who says
the burnt offering that Israel brought in the desert
phrases.notes: This refers to the offerings brought at סיני (שמות 24:5).

phrases.english: was the daily burnt offering.
And from all of them together, too, it cannot be learned,
since they all existed before the Divine speech!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמִּילָה וְתָמִיד — שֶׁכֵּן יֶשְׁנוֹ לִפְנֵי הַדִּבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the last pair and the three-way combination, closing the search
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects מילה+תמיד and all three together
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: All of them were commanded before מתן תורה, a special status that יבום lacks
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the attempt to answer the question of step 9 from these cases, so the גמרא must find a new explanation for why עליה is needed.

steps.title: עליה is needed because of honoring parents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes approach: the word עליה is needed, because we might have thought to learn from כיבוד אב ואם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is needed. You might have thought to learn it from honoring father and mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on מילה, פסח and תמיד and answers the question of step 9 differently. The verse עליה is needed because otherwise we might have learned from כיבוד אב ואם. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why the תורה needed to write עליה, if no source shows an עשה pushing aside a כרת prohibition. The new answer: there is a possible source we would have used, כיבוד אב ואם. So the verse was needed to block that learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, a signal that the גמרא is taking a new approach
It was necessary
It might enter your mind to say, introducing a mistaken assumption
The מצוה to honor one's father and mother

steps.whatToRemember: No combination of מילה, פסח and תמיד works, since each has a special feature. The גמרא now says עליה was needed because we might have learned from כיבוד אב ואם.

phrases.english: Rather, it is needed.
phrases.notes: He means the word עליה really is needed.

phrases.english: It could enter your mind to say

steps.title: The ברייתא about honoring parents and שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that without a פסוק, we would have thought כיבוד אב ואם overrides שבת. The פסוק teaches that parent and child alike must honor ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: You might think honoring your father and mother pushes aside שבת. That is why the פסוק says: 'Every man shall fear his mother and his father, and you shall keep My שבתות.' This means all of you, parent and child, must honor Me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up what it said in step 16, that we might have learned from כיבוד אב ואם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא admits there was a real reason to think כיבוד אב ואם would override שבת. The תורה puts both מצות in one פסוק to block that idea: the parent is also commanded to honor ה׳, so the child may not break שבת for the parent.

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the idea in step 16 that we might have learned from כיבוד אב ואם. The rest of the discussion turns on how far it reaches.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as cooking and slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is talking about a father who asks for real שבת labor. That would show a מצות עשה could override a כרת-level prohibition if there were no פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא talking about a father who told his son: 'Slaughter for me, cook for me'? Then the only reason it is forbidden is that the תורה wrote 'Keep My שבתות.' So without that פסוק, honoring parents would override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to pull a big rule out of the ברייתא: a מצות עשה can push aside even a prohibition that carries כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering and cooking are full מלאכות of שבת, which carry כרת. If only the פסוק stops כיבוד אב ואם from overriding them, then normally a מצות עשה would override even a כרת prohibition. The words 'הא לאו הכי' mean 'but if not for this פסוק.'

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (opens a suggested reading)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a child may cook on שבת for a parent. The ברייתא clearly forbids it. The question is only what we would have thought without the פסוק.

phrases.english: Is it not where his father said to him:
Slaughter for me, cook for me,
and the reason is that the Merciful One wrote
"Keep My Shabbatot",

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא from step 17 as covering full שבת labors and draws a general rule from it.
steps.raayaObject: That a מצות עשה would override even a prohibition carrying כרת if there were no פסוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the ברייתא in step 17, read as a case of slaughtering and cooking

steps.title: The גמרא begins to reject that reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers 'No' and starts to push back on reading the ברייתא as cooking and slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts rejecting the proof from step 18. This one word sets up the next move, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'No', the גמרא signals that the ברייתא does not have to be about כרת-level labor. So the big rule from step 18 is not yet proven.
